advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct unit test for is_missing_ref() asserting each of the three markers -> True and a transport/auth stderr -> False.
evidence: src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py:178 `_MISSING_REF_STDERR_MARKERS = ( "couldn't find remote ref", "no such ref", "not our ref", )`
search of tests for `is_missing_ref` returned `(no matches)`
Adjacent existing test `test_auth_marker_detection` (tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py:207) directly pins is_auth_failure markers but there is no parallel test for is_missing_ref.
advisory.finding: The new is_missing_ref() function and its three stderr markers ("couldn't find remote ref", "no such ref", "not our ref") have no direct unit test asserting each marker returns True and a transport/auth marker returns False. Coverage is only end-to-end via one real-git missing-ref case, so a regression that drops/mistypes one of the additional markers (e.g. 'not our ref') would not be caught unless a test happens to hit that exact git wording.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized test mirroring test_auth_marker_detection: assert is_missing_ref matches each marker string and rejects an auth/transport stderr.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that the scoped opening fetch failing with a non-missing-ref (transport/auth) stderr re-raises SnapshotFetchError from resolve_ref.
evidence: src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:278 `except SnapshotFetchError as exc:` / :279 `if not is_missing_ref(exc.stderr): raise`
The new file's fail-closed test (test_unresolvable_ref_still_fails_closed) expects SnapshotRefError (the degrade branch), not SnapshotFetchError (the re-raise branch).
Commit message: 'a transport/auth/stall/timeout fetch failure is re-raised' — this half is not pinned in the new suite.
advisory.finding: The within-diff fail-closed re-raise branch of resolve_ref (`except SnapshotFetchError as exc: if not is_missing_ref(exc.stderr): raise`) is not exercised by the new regression file; the new file only pins the degrade-to-SnapshotRefError path. The transport-failure-re-raise contract emphasized in the commit message relies solely on the pre-existing test_missing_credential_fetch_raises_descriptive_error, which is a materialize()/nonexistent-remote scenario rather than a scoped-fetch transport failure.
advisory.suggested_fix: Point the clone's origin at an unreachable/nonexistent remote and assert rs.resolve_ref("origin/main", ...) raises SnapshotFetchError (not SnapshotRefError).
